atlas.name: Yeo 7 resting-state networks (Yeo et al. 2011)
atlas.description: Seven cortical networks obtained by clustering resting-state functional connectivity of 1000 subjects.

reference.text: Yeo BTT et al. (2011). The organization of the human cerebral cortex estimated by intrinsic functional connectivity. J Neurophysiol 106, 1125-1165.

atlas.data_source: fsLR 32k dlabel file from the CBIG GitHub repository (ThomasYeoLab/CBIG).
atlas.note: Network names follow the common usage of Yeo et al. 2011; descriptions summarise the cited reviews.

Visual.location: Occipital lobe, extending into posterior temporal and parietal cortex.

Somatomotor.location: Pre- and postcentral gyri, extending into auditory cortex.
Somatomotor.function: Motor and somatosensory cortex; in the 7-network solution auditory cortex is included as well.

Dorsal attention.location: Intraparietal sulcus, superior parietal lobule, frontal eye fields and MT+.
Dorsal attention.function: Top-down, goal-directed control of spatial attention.

references.text: Corbetta M, Shulman GL (2002). Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain. Nat Rev Neurosci 3, 201-215.

Ventral attention.location: Temporo-parietal junction, ventral frontal cortex, anterior insula and dorsal anterior cingulate.
Ventral attention.function: Stimulus-driven reorienting of attention. Overlaps with the 'salience' and 'cingulo-opercular' networks described by other groups.

references.text: Corbetta M, Shulman GL (2002). Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain. Nat Rev Neurosci 3, 201-215.
Seeley WW et al. (2007). Dissociable intrinsic connectivity networks for salience processing and executive control. J Neurosci 27, 2349-2356.

Limbic.function: Functionally heterogeneous. fMRI signal in these regions suffers from susceptibility artefacts, so the network boundaries are less reliable than elsewhere.

Frontoparietal.location: Lateral prefrontal cortex, anterior inferior parietal lobule and part of the precuneus.
Frontoparietal.function: Cognitive control and executive function; flexibly couples with the default and dorsal attention networks depending on task demands.

references.text: Vincent JL et al. (2008). Evidence for a frontoparietal control system revealed by intrinsic functional connectivity. J Neurophysiol 100, 3328-3342.

Default.location: Medial prefrontal cortex, posterior cingulate/precuneus, angular gyrus and lateral temporal cortex.
Default.function: More active at rest than during externally directed tasks; linked to self-referential thought, memory retrieval and mental simulation.

references.text: Raichle ME et al. (2001). A default mode of brain function. PNAS 98, 676-682.
Buckner RL, Andrews-Hanna JR, Schacter DL (2008). The brain's default network: anatomy, function, and relevance to disease. Ann N Y Acad Sci 1124, 1-38.
